escalation: Class 11 wrong-link-target: the anchor for the feminine participle, display כַּרְיָא, targets 'Jastrow, כַּרְיָא I 1' (K01154, ch. of כְּרִי 'heap, pile', whose own plural_form is כַּרְוָון). The consonantal skeleton כריא carries two headwords vocalized identically, K01154 כַּרְיָא I and K01155 כַּרְיָא II, and it is II ('a worm in poppy') that itself opens '(cmp. כְּרַהּ)' pointing back at this entry; the niqqud carve-out cannot separate them and the Roman numeral is the only distinguishing byte, so a maintainer must pick the intended target. Display text כַּרְיָא / target כַּרְיָא I. Not repairable: the corrected data-ref bytes ('II') are not present in the entry. Judged and accepted as correct, for the record: the pl. anchor כְּרִין -> 'Jastrow, כרים 1' is legitimate, K01168 כרים records כְּרִין in its alt_headwords and redirects back here.

The entry's refs[] preserves 'Berakhot 44b:9' and 'Berakhot 44b:10', which no anchor in the entry uses, so the first anchor most likely lost its own segment and inherited the second's. Anomaly hint abbrev-mislink accepted — class 11 wrong-link-target: display כְּרוֹ׳ in '(Y. כְּרוּזָא, some ed. כְּרוֹ׳)' abbreviates this entry's own headword כָּרוֹז ² / alt כְּרוּזָא (it is a manuscript variant of the Targum word under discussion) but targets 'Jastrow, כְּרוֹבָא 1' (K01105, 'dug around, marked off'), which shares only the opening letters. Not repairable: the correct data-ref bytes are not present. Second finding, needs the printed page: the citation 'Y. Ned. lV, 38ᵈ top' has a lowercase L standing for the Roman numeral I ('lV' for 'IV'); correcting it needs a byte outside the closed marker grammar. (Corpus-wide this OCR l-for-I substitution in Roman numerals is rare — about six instances — so it is reported here rather than as a systemic shape.)
